title: The Great Seed Scramble
markdown:
The sun burst through the window and painted stripes on the floor. It tickled Ivo’s nose. “Morning already?” His tiny mechanic fingers twitched. Today was the Seed Scramble: a race across the fields to find the most interesting seeds, not merely the most.

“Ready, little bolt?” Grandad Sol boomed. His beard was like moonlight.

“Born ready.” Ivo bounced and adjusted his goggles. Being tiny still sat in his chest — a screw trying to keep up with bolts.

A shadow swooped. Nyx the raven landed on his shoulder, feathers like dark glass. “Don’t fret. Smarts over speed. You’ve got plenty.”

A gust whooshed the garden. Seeds danced: fluffy parachutes, tiny hooks, little rockets. “They’re everywhere!”

“Precisely,” Sol chuckled. “The race has begun. Let’s see who can gather the most wonderful travelers.”

They dashed. The field was a green carpet. Ivo, with Nyx guiding, spotted seeds clinging to tall grasses. “Hooks! Tiny grappling irons!” Nyx dipped and weaved; a few hooked seeds caught on her feathers. “They grab on, like anchors.”

Ahead, milkweed puffed white. Fluffy tufts rode the breeze. “Parachutes!” Ivo grabbed a large leaf. “Push them toward it!” Nyx flapped; seeds landed. Gotcha.

A sharp pop. Oxalis pods sprung open, flinging seeds like projectiles. “Exploding pods. Seed fireworks.” Ivo ducked and scooped a few that had not gone far.

They raced past a pond. Smooth round seeds bobbed. “They float. Tiny boats.”

Sol watched, smiling. “You’re not just racing.”

Their collection grew: sticky coats, berry-like fruit, seeds that rode the wind like kites. Ivo’s sharp eyes and Nyx’s aerial view found a sticky seed on a thistle. He nudged it onto a smooth leaf Nyx spotted. Plink. It stuck.

Under an oak, the morning’s buzz softening, Sol turned a hooked seed in his fingers. “Hitch a ride. Float. Burst. Wear a tasty coat. Each one is trying to find a new spot to grow.”

Ivo looked at the pile: miniature marvels, sorted roughly by how they had travelled. “Hooks, fluff, fruit, exploding pods.”

“Nature spreading life,” Sol said, and stopped before calling it a spectacular show. He tucked a parachute seed into Ivo’s tin so it would not blow back into the race.

Ivo grinned. He had not outrun anyone. He had noticed. He did not declare the day amazing or the adventure beginning. He tightened a loose goggle strap, counted the tin once more, and let Nyx steal a single hooked seed for her feathers, which was, after all, how that kind preferred to travel.
